title: Exception
description: exception/v1 — the document an exception event carries. The executing organization declares that a leg of this report cannot complete, which parks the report: its deadline is held while the exception is open, so it is never settled incomplete in the middle of being answered. Raised by any participant: the organization that ran the leg is the only one that can tell a failure from a transfer still settling, since execution records are organization-private and never replicated, while the valuation engine is the side that knows a report can no longer be covered in time. A report may carry several open exceptions at once, one per failed leg. The event itself cites the report's authoring event in its reference list.

exceptionId.description: Identity of this exception, minted by the facade. A manual resolve answers it by this id, and cites its event in the reference list.

reportId.description: The report whose execution cannot complete.

status.description: Always `open` as authored. Like a margin report's own `new`, it never changes on the log — every organization derives the live value from what answers it, so all of them fold the same answer.

blame.description: The role whose SIDE the problem is on — not an allocation of fault. A container ledger being unavailable is the controller's side without being anyone's mistake.

reason.description: Why the leg cannot complete, in the raiser's own words. Shown to the counterparty, who decides what to do about it.

raisedBy.description: The organization raising it. Events carry roles rather than organizations, so the document pins the organization for readers and authority checks.

executionPlanId.description: The plan that failed, when there was one. Diagnostic: the raiser is the only party that can see its own execution records.

quantity.description: The shortfall, as a decimal string.
